bib.title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks

question: Can a conditional GAN with a learned loss serve as a general-purpose solution to image-to-image translation (pixels to pixels) across many tasks without per-task loss engineering?
hypothesis: A discriminator-learned loss penalises structure that hand-designed per-pixel losses (L1/L2) miss and avoids blur; L1 handles low frequencies while a patch-level GAN handles high frequencies.
contributions: Demonstrate that on a wide variety of problems, conditional GANs produce reasonable results.
Present a simple framework sufficient to achieve good results, and analyze the effects of several important architectural choices.

method.summary: A conditional GAN (pix2pix): a U-Net generator G and a 70x70 PatchGAN discriminator D that sees (input, output) pairs, trained with the cGAN loss plus lambda*L1 on paired data. The same architecture and objective are retrained on each dataset; ablations cover loss, generator architecture and patch size, evaluated by AMT real-vs-fake tests and an FCN-score on Cityscapes.
method.task: paired image-to-image translation (labels to photo, map to aerial, colorization, edges to photo, day to night, thermal to color, inpainting, photo to labels)

datasets.name: Cityscapes labels<->photo
datasets.split: Cityscapes training set for training, validation set for testing
datasets.preprocessing: 256x256; random jitter (resize to 286x286, random crop 256x256) and mirroring

datasets.name: Maps<->aerial (Google Maps, NYC)
datasets.split: split about the median latitude of the sampling region, with a buffer so no training pixel appears in test
datasets.source: scraped from Google Maps in and around New York City
datasets.preprocessing: 256x256 train, tested at 512x512; random jitter and mirroring

datasets.name: BW->color (ImageNet)
datasets.split: subset of ImageNet val set, following protocol of Zhang et al. 2016 and Larsson et al. 2016

datasets.name: Edges->shoes (UT Zappos50K)
datasets.source: Yu and Grauman 2014; edges by HED plus postprocessing

datasets.name: Paris StreetView inpainting
datasets.split: 100 held-out test images following Pathak et al.

models.name: pix2pix generator, U-Net
models.architecture: encoder-decoder with skip connections between layer i and n-i (concatenation); 4x4 convs stride 2; dropout 50% in decoder

other.output: conv to 3 channels (2 for colorization) then Tanh; no BatchNorm on first C64; leaky ReLU 0.2 in encoder, plain ReLU in decoder

models.name: PatchGAN discriminator 70x70
models.architecture: fully convolutional, classifies each NxN patch, responses averaged

other.layers: C64-C128-C256-C512 then conv to 1-d output and Sigmoid
other.note: no BatchNorm on first C64; leaky ReLU 0.2

other.use: scores synthesized photos by segmentation accuracy against the labels they came from

training.objective: G* = arg min_G max_D L_cGAN(G,D) + lambda*L_L1(G), lambda=100; G trained to maximise log D(x,G(x,z)) rather than minimise log(1-D); D objective divided by 2
training.optimizer: Adam, minibatch SGD, alternating one D step then one G step
training.batch_size: 1 to 10 depending on experiment (1 Cityscapes objective experiments, 10 for U-Net vs encoder-decoder; 4 for BW->color, edges->shoes/handbags, day->night, thermal, inpainting)
training.dropout: 50% in decoder CD layers, kept on at test time (the only noise source)
training.regularisation: random jitter and mirroring; no explicit noise z
training.compute: facade results (Fig 14) took less than two hours of training
training.wall_clock: less than two hours for the 400-image facade set

other.batchnorm_at_test: test-batch statistics (instance norm when batch size 1)
other.errata: with batch size 1 the BatchNorm zeroes the bottleneck activations, effectively skipping the innermost layer; public code removes BatchNorm there

inference.decoding: deterministic forward pass of G in training mode: dropout on, BatchNorm with test-batch statistics
inference.samples: one output per input; only minor stochasticity from dropout

parameters.test_resolution: fully convolutional: train 256x256, test 512x512 on maps<->aerial

other.time: all models run in well under a second on a Pascal Titan X

metrics.name: AMT real vs fake
metrics.definition: Turkers see a real and a generated image for 1 second each, then pick the fake; 40 main trials after 10 practice trials with feedback; ~50 Turkers per algorithm; one algorithm per session; no vigilance trials

metrics.name: FCN-score
metrics.definition: FCN-8s trained on Cityscapes classifies synthesized photos; accuracy against the labels they were generated from
metrics.unit: per-pixel acc., per-class acc., class IOU (fractions 0-1)

metrics.name: Histogram intersection of Lab colour marginals vs ground truth
metrics.definition: overlap of output colour distributions with ground-truth distributions

baselines: L2 regression from Zhang et al. 2016
Pathak et al. 2016 context encoders (inpainting, qualitative)
eval.protocol: Single training run per configuration; no seeds or confidence intervals for FCN-scores. Bootstrap test for AMT significance. Colorization AMT real and fake generated from the same grayscale input; map<->aerial real and fake from different inputs. FCN-scores recomputed in v2 with scripts at phillipi/pix2pix scripts/eval_cityscapes commit d7e7b8b.

availability.data: public datasets; maps data scraped from Google Maps (release not stated)

evidence.quote: we use batch sizes between 1 and 10 depending on the experiment
took less than two hours of training on a single Pascal Titan X GPU

results.claim: An unconditional discriminator (GAN) collapses to near-identical outputs regardless of input and scores poorly.

results.table: Table 1, row GAN, column Per-pixel acc.

results.claim: U-Net beats encoder-decoder under L1+cGAN; the encoder-decoder gets worse when the cGAN term is added.

Adversarial loss helps aerial-photo generation from maps: 18.9% of trials fooled Turkers versus nearly none for L1.

limits: Requires paired training data; no unpaired setting is explored.
Output is only mildly stochastic: noise z was ignored by G, so dropout is the only noise; capturing the full conditional entropy is left open.
cGANs hallucinate small objects in segmentation and L1 alone scores better on photo->labels.
Colorization falls short of the task-specific method of Zhang et al. (22.5% vs 27.8%); photo->map not significantly better than L1.
Common failure modes: artifacts where input is sparse, unusual inputs, grayscale or desaturated colorizations (Figs 9, 21).
Single training runs and no seeds reported for FCN-scores; the authors note run-to-run variation (Table 2 caption).
Batch-size-1 BatchNorm zeroes the bottleneck layer (errata); the authors left experiments as is.
Community applications (Sec 4.7) are uncontrolled and may rely on modified code.
FCN-score and AMT are weak proxies; FID and later metrics did not exist.

terms.definition: a discriminator that tries to classify if each NxN patch in an image is real or fake, run convolutionally across the image with responses averaged
accuracy of an FCN-8s segmenter trained on real Cityscapes, scored on synthesized photos against the labels they were generated from
losses that penalize the joint configuration of the output rather than treating pixels as conditionally independent

consistent with finding that generator ignores noise
